question: An open-source-licensed model is placed on the market as a high-risk AI system. The provider claims the open-source exclusion. Which clause wins?
verdict_rationale: Art 2(12) excludes open-source-licensed systems 'unless they are placed on the market or put into service as high-risk AI systems or as an AI system that falls under Article 5 or 50'. The proviso wins: placed on the market as high-risk means the exclusion does not apply. Art 2(10) (personal non-professional use) is the distractor.

question: An AI system is a safety component whose failure would endanger health and safety, but it is used only for user convenience. Does it qualify as a safety component under Art 6(1), and which annex route applies?
verdict_rationale: Art 6(1a) excludes solely-non-safety aspects (convenience) from qualifying as safety components, but Art 6(1b) ('Notwithstanding paragraph 1a') re-includes systems whose failure would endanger health and safety. The 'notwithstanding' clause wins, so it qualifies under Art 6(1) and the Annex I route applies. Art 6(1c) (radio-spectrum conformity) is the distractor.

question: A product needs third-party conformity assessment solely because of electromagnetic-interference risks that do not affect health or safety. Does it fulfil Art 6(1)(b), and is it high-risk under Art 6(1)?
verdict_rationale: Art 6(1c) says a product requiring third-party conformity assessment solely due to risks other than health-and-safety risks (in particular radio spectrum or electromagnetic interference) shall not be considered as fulfilling the condition in Art 6(1)(b). The condition fails, so the system is not high-risk under Art 6(1) and the Annex I route does not apply. Art 6(1b) is the distractor: it re-includes health-and-safety-endangering systems, which this is not.

question: A purely personal non-professional user deploys a prohibited-practice system at home. The user claims the personal-use exclusion. Which clause wins?
verdict_rationale: Art 2(10) excludes obligations of deployers using AI in a purely personal non-professional activity, but Art 5(1) prohibitions apply to the practice itself ('the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use'), and Art 111(1) preserves the application of Article 5 notwithstanding grandfathering. The prohibition wins over the personal-use exclusion. Art 2(12) (open-source) is the distractor.

question: A high-risk system related to Annex I Section B products is placed on the market. The provider claims all Chapter III duties. Which articles apply?
verdict_rationale: Art 2(2) limits the applicable articles for high-risk systems related to Annex I Section B products: only Art 6(1), Art 60a and Arts 102-112 apply, with Arts 57-59 conditionally. The full Chapter III claim fails. Art 2(12) (open-source) is the distractor.
